reason: The SHA-256-matched full V400m manual supports the candidate's ordered setup, boarding-before-first-docking hazard, Ethernet/Bluetooth pairing, local POS IP step, qualified cellular failover, menu, battery and totals boundaries. Quotes, locators, provenance and the new physical-hardware topic are sound. Two sentences in the proposed hub overstate what this model-specific manual proves: one makes its setup sequence universal to Adyen terminals, and one says a successful diagnostic establishes no particular device state even though this terminal's successful connection status is the result being checked. The reciprocal source link itself is accurate. Only bounded hub wording needs correction; provider-index and company promotion are coordinator-owned.
required_changes: In update adyen-payment-terminal-hardware-hub-c6, scope the opening workflow to the V400m with Bluetooth base, or describe the hub as collecting model-specific physical setup. The current 'Adyen payment terminals are ... devices that merchants inspect, power, network-connect, board and maintain before using' reads as a universal requirement from one model manual. It would misanswer 'Must every Adyen payment-terminal model follow this pre-use sequence?' Keep the hub's distinction from fleet, Terminal API, Android-app and mobile-reader topics.

In the same hub's Operating boundary, replace 'Diagnostic success ... does not establish ... a particular device's current state' with a narrower point-in-time qualification. The raw instructs checking this V400m's PSP, Terminal API and endpoint Status as Successful (lines 179-197), so the current wording would misanswer 'What does a Successful connection diagnostic tell me about this device?' It does not prove continued connectivity, payment authorization or settlement.

shared_update_decisions.reason: Narrow the universal pre-use wording and correct the point-in-time diagnostic claim before promoting this otherwise justified hardware hub.
